html:
The Kooma are an Aboriginal Australian people of the border region of Queensland and New South Wales, around the Balonne and Culgoa rivers. Today the name describes a grouping of families descended from the Koamu and related tribes of the area.

Their neighbours were the Muruwari to the south, the Gunya to the west and the Gunggari, Bigambul and Mandandanji to the north and east. Sheep and cattle runs reached these rivers in the 1840s and 1850s.
